    MAT-21 — history¶

    Opened 2026-10-12 by the 18:00 daily review under §9 rule (5) lane 3 (Phases 7/8), for tonight's weekly to ratify. Phase 8 (8a) is the closed-form lane (MAT-9 … MAT-20), and MAT-15 step 2 checked the finite Robin cylinder against its eigen-series. §10 (8e) names an ASTM-style gel phantom, and PROJECT_PLAN.md line 4814 gives the F2182 phantom as 650 × 420 × 90 mm. That phantom is a rectangular box, and the lane has no box. MAT-21 is the box version of MAT-15 step 2: the same gel, Robin walls and a uniform source, solved as a triple eigen-series and then by P1 FEM on a structured create_box mesh.

    Source. Carslaw & Jaeger, Conduction of Heat in Solids: the rectangular parallelepiped by product solutions of three slab problems. The book is not held in-repo. docs/references/ holds Jin's FEM in Electromagnetics (jin-fem-3e/, which has no heat conduction), the birdcage-tuning literature, human body models and the dolfinx-0.11 migration notes. As with MAT-15 (analytical.py:1950, "Carslaw & Jaeger ch. III / VIII style; derived here, not pinned to a textbook equation"), the citation is a pointer and no chapter or equation number is claimed. The docstring derives every identity the test asserts. The in-repo cross-checks are the real test: - Robin residuals on all six faces; - the Gauss balance ∮hθ dA = qV, in its truncated-identity form; - a second route that is exact in z; - Duhamel; - the large-lateral limit, which must reach the 1-D slab closed form q(C² − z²)/(2k) + qC/h; - cube permutation symmetry; - transient → steady at long t; - the initial slope dθ/dt|₀ = q/ρc in the interior.

    Its pieces are already in-repo. robin_slab_eigenvalues and _robin_slab_coefficients (src/fem_em_solver/utils/analytical.py:1874–1940) were checked by MAT-15 step 2(a) at Bi_z 0.667 (20261001T143248Z_MAT-15-step2a-W1b.log:85–86).

    Fixture numbers (stdlib-only Python arithmetic for this brief, not a harness run; every value below is predicted). - Half-widths A = 0.325, B = 0.21, C = 0.045 m (650 × 420 × 90 mm halved). V = 8ABC = 0.02457 m³; surface area A_s = 0.7386 m². - Gel constants as in MAT-15: k 0.6, ρc 4.18e6, h 10, q 2000, T∞ = T(0) = 20. - Biot numbers hL/k: Bi_x = 5.4167, Bi_y = 3.5000, Bi_z = 0.7500. First roots γ₁ = 1.330018 / 1.232272 / 0.771359. - Time scales: α = k/ρc = 1.4354e-7 m²/s; t_C = C²ρc/k = 14 107.5 s. Slowest mode: Λ₁₁₁ = 345.005 m⁻², τ₁ = 1/(αΛ₁₁₁) = 20 193 s. - Steady centre θ_ss(0): - 12.003947 K at n = (40, 40, 40); - 12.003956 K at (60, 60, 60); - 12.003958 K by the z-reduced route at (160, 160); - the slab limit is 12.375 K, so lateral cooling takes off ≈ 3.0 %. - Steady values elsewhere: corner (A, B, C) 2.5526 K; face centres x / y / z 6.1505 / 6.2367 / 8.7340 K; mean surface θ = qV/(hA_s) = 6.6531 K. - Transient centre: θ(0, 0.2 t_C) = 1.335705 K, against qt/ρc = 1.35 K; θ(0, t_C) = 5.511718 K.

    §9 item 406 — 2026-10-12 (lane 3, closed form)¶

    MAT-21 step 0: the rectangular gel box with Robin walls under a uniform source, as a triple eigen-series in numpy only. - Executor and tier: implementer; smoke, no MPI, real build. - Change: src/ additive, plus one new test. - Time: ≈ 12 measured / 40 predicted min (≈ 2 min of windows + 15 fixed + ≈ 23 code). - Depends on nothing.

    • Anchor (derive in the docstring). θ = T − T∞ on the box |x| ≤ A, |y| ≤ B, |z| ≤ C, with −k∂ₙθ = hθ on all six faces and a uniform q.
    • 1-D pieces. For each axis d with half-width L_d and Bi_d = hL_d/k: γ_{d,n} are the roots of γ sin γ = Bi_d cos γ, and X_{d,n}(s) = cos(γ_{d,n} s/L_d). Each X_{d,n} satisfies the Robin condition at s = ±L_d. C_{d,n} = 2 sin γ/(γ + sin γ cos γ) is the projection of 1 (_robin_slab_coefficients).
    • Expansion of 1. The product basis X_l(x)Y_m(y)Z_n(z) is orthogonal on the box, so 1 = Σ C_l C_m C_n X_l Y_m Z_n.
    • Steady state. ∇²(XYZ) = −Λ·XYZ with Λ_lmn = (γ_l/A)² + (γ_m/B)² + (γ_n/C)². Hence θ_ss = (q/k) Σ C_l C_m C_n X_l Y_m Z_n / Λ_lmn.
    • Transient with a uniform start θ₀ = t_init − T∞: θ(t) = Σ C_l C_m C_n X Y Z [(q/(kΛ))·(−expm1(−αΛt)) + θ₀ e^{−αΛt}], α = k/ρc. From θ₀ = 0 this is the task's form θ_ss × (1 − e^{−αΛt}) term by term.
    • Truncated identities. The truncated sum satisfies two identities exactly.
      • Gauss: h∮θ_N dA = qV·Π_d S_d(N_d), where S_d = Σ_{n ≤ N_d} C_{d,n} sin γ_{d,n}/γ_{d,n}. This is Parseval: h∮θ_N = −k∫∇²θ_N = q∫P_N 1.
      • Duhamel: θ(t) = (q/ρc)∫₀ᵗ U_x U_y U_z ds, where U_d(s, ·) = Σ C_{d,n} X_{d,n} e^{−α(γ_{d,n}/L_d)² s}, at the same truncation.
    • Code. Append to src/fem_em_solver/utils/analytical.py directly after robin_finite_cylinder_transient_temperature (ends ≈ line 2034), under a new MAT-21 step 0 banner and before the MAT-17 step 1 banner (≈ line 2037). The change is additive and reorders nothing.
    • robin_box_steady_temperature(x, y, z, *, half_widths, k, q, h, t_inf=0.0, n_terms=(40, 40, 40), roots=None, return_gradient=False). It returns T, or (T, (∂ₓT, ∂ᵧT, ∂_zT)) when return_gradient is set.
    • robin_box_transient_temperature(x, y, z, t, *, half_widths, k, q, h, rho_c, t_inf=0.0, t_init=None, n_terms=(40, 40, 40), roots=None, return_gradient=False). The default t_init is T∞.
    • roots is a 3-tuple of None or an array per axis, for the negative control only. An overridden axis takes its length from the array, and C is the same projection formula at those roots (as radial_roots works for the cylinder).
    • Both functions share one private contraction, _robin_box_sum(W, x, y, z, …). It is separable and done in BLAS, never as a 3-index einsum over points. Form R = X(P × N_x) @ W.reshape(N_x, N_y·N_z), then multiply by Y and reduce over m, then dot with Z.
    • The function chunks internally so that the (P × N_y·N_z) intermediate stays ≤ 2²² doubles (32 MiB). Every caller (step 1's P2 interpolation included) is safe without chunking of its own.
    • Steady and transient use the same truncated term set, so t → ∞ returns θ_ss to round-off.
    • Constants: test module tests/validation/test_mat21_box_closed_form.py, which imports K, RHO_C, H, Q and T_INF from tests/validation/test_mat15_finite_cylinder_closed_form.py. Do not restate them.
    • Module constants:
      • A_BOX, B_BOX, C_BOX = 0.325, 0.21, 0.045, with a comment citing PROJECT_PLAN.md:4814 (650 × 420 × 90 mm, halved);
      • HALF;
      • T_C = C_BOX**2 * RHO_C / K;
      • FOS = (0.05, 0.2, 1.0);
      • SERIES_TERMS = (40, 40, 40).
    • Anchors (asserted). Each bar is either a closed-form identity at round-off or MAT-15 step 2(a)'s pre-registered bar of the same form, as written in test_mat15_finite_cylinder_closed_form.py: (R0) roots and coefficients at :95–97, (R1) Robin residual at :116, (R5) limits at :229–231.
    • (R0) Roots and coefficients.
      • For Bi ∈ {Bi_x, Bi_y, Bi_z}, 400 roots, each in ((n − 1)π, (n − ½)π). Residual |γ sin γ − Bi cos γ|/γ ≤ 1e-12.
      • C in the two closed forms, 2 sin γ/(γ + sin γ cos γ) and 2Bi cos γ(γ² + Bi²)/(γ²(γ² + Bi² + Bi)). They must agree to ≤ 1e-12 in the series norm max|ΔC|/max|C|. The per-root relative difference is printed only: see Traps.
    • (R1) Robin residuals on all six faces.
      • Sample points: a 7 × 7 grid over [−0.95, 0.95] of the two tangential half-widths on each face.
      • Analytic gradients; |−k∂ₙθ − hθ|/(qC) ≤ 1e-10.
      • Run for steady and for transient at t = Fo·t_C, Fo ∈ FOS.

This brief sets no band and moves none: D_BAND, L_BAND, INTERIOR_BAND, E_BAND are imported by name as in item 424, and D_BAND is not widened. - Why (the ruling's diagnosis, checked against the parked log). - The definitions. As posed, (FEM) = maxᵢ|aᵢ − bᵢ|/max|a|. Here a = running_average(t, duty) and b = Σ(−1)^m running_average(t, H_m), as at test_mat21_box_duty_fem.py:115–121 on the branch. - running_average is linear in its input series (src/fem_em_solver/thermal/dose.py:108–174). Its steps are: - the cumulative integral is a trapezoid cumsum of 0.5(vₖ + vₖ₊₁)Δtₖ (:155–156); - the window-start value is a linear interpolation v_j + a(v_{j+1} − v_j), whose fraction a depends only on t and W (:162–164); - the partial-segment integral F_j + (s − t_j)·0.5(v_j + v_s) is linear (:165); - the means are (F[idx] − F_s)/W (:168).

    Every coefficient depends only on (t, W). The max / argmax at `:169–171` are not linear, but (FEM) uses only the means.
    • So (FEM) inherits (H0)'s residual through a window mean. a − b = running_average(t, r), with rₙ = ⟨θ_duty⟩ₙ − Σ(−1)^m⟨θ_Hm⟩ₙ. This r is the per-step Duhamel residual that (H0) gates at L_BAND. Each window mean is a convex combination of r's samples, so |a − b| ≤ maxₙ|rₙ|.
    • The parked numbers (20261013T183523Z_MAT-21-step2-W2-identities.log):
      • The H_m means are large. H₀'s mean at t* is the step response, 1.23889 K (20261013T183409Z_MAT-21-step2-W1.log:71), against a duty mean that peaks at max|duty| = 0.624543 K (n = 36, W2 :117).
      • (H0) read 3.799e-13 relative to max|duty| (:119), so max|r| ≈ 3.799e-13 × 0.624543 = 2.373e-13 K.
      • (FEM) read 1.4637e-13 relative to max|a| = 0.61668 K (:121, :124, :142), which is 9.03e-14 K absolute. That is under max|r| by 2.6×, as the bound requires.
      • The ceiling max|r|/max|a| is therefore ≈ 3.85e-13, above D_BAND 1e-13.

    The profile (chosen while drafting), and why. q(x) = Q·[1 − cos(πx/A)], with q_y = q_z = 1. - The end-ring signature. The source is zero at the centre and 2Q at the x-ends (x = ±A, 650 mm apart). - Total power unchanged. The mean over [−A, A] is exactly Q, so ∫q dV = QV = 49.14 W, as in steps 1–5, and the Gauss comparand Q·V_h is step 3's formula unchanged. - Non-negative, and even in x. So only the existing cos(γs/L) Robin family is needed. An odd or shifted profile would need the sin family (roots of γ cot γ = −Bi), which is new code and not taken. - One full period on [−A, A], which is what keeps the FEM's balances at round-off (see FEM side). - Rejected: q = Q·[1 + cos(πx/A)] (centre-peaked). It is the same work, but it is not the end-ring signature. - Rejected: a quadratic profile. It would avoid every quadrature question, but it is not P32's "cosine profile".

    The closed form (Anchor 1, W1). - Projection, in closed form. ∫_{−L}^{L} cos(as) cos(bs) ds = 2[a sin(aL) cos(bL) − b cos(aL) sin(bL)]/(a² − b²). - With a = jπ/L and b = γ/L this is 2L(−1)^{j+1} γ sin γ/((jπ)² − γ²). - Divide by ∫cos²(γs/L) ds = L(γ + sin γ cos γ)/γ to get D^{(j)} = (−1)^{j+1} C γ²/((jπ)² − γ²), with C = 2 sin γ/(γ + sin γ cos γ) (analytical.py:1937–1940). - At j = 0, D^{(0)} = C. For this source, P = C − D^{(1)} = C(π² − 2γ²)/(π² − γ²). - There is no pole. γ lies i((n − 1)π, (n − ½)π) (:1880), so it never equals jπ for Bi > 0. At n = j + 1 the gap is γ − jπ ≈ Bi/(jπ), so D stays O(1). - Drafting values (stdlib Python, x-axis, Bi 5.4167): γ 1.330018 / 4.068213 / 6.945535; C 1.243794 / −0.351594 / 0.165527; D 0.271608 / 0.871010 / −0.208103; P 0.972185 / −1.222604 / 0.373630. - Steady:** θ_ss = (Q) Σ P C_m C_n X_l Y_m/Λ_lmn, the step 0 form (:2129–2131) with C_l → P_l.     The FEM side (Anchor 2, W2). - Rung: m = 4, create_box (52, 32, 8) with 79 872 cells. P2: 116 025 dofs; P3 comparand: 380 725 points (step 3 W1 :105). - m = 6 is out of scope. Its 9.94 GiB RSS was a steady-only reading. - On m = 4, step 3's mask, χ and comparand construction carry over exactly, so (U) is a same-mask, same-rung prior. - The source is a UFL expression: xs = ufl.SpatialCoordinate(msh); q_sep = Q * (1.0 - ufl.cos(ufl.pi * xs[0] / A_BOX)). - It is passed as q= to both solvers. _as_source uses an expression as-is (thermal/steady.py:63–68; transient.py:208). - No ufl.conditional, no max_value, no ordering comparison, no sqrt. The build is complex, as in steps 1–5. - Why the balances stay at round-off (the trap this profile defuses, found while drafting). - The solvers integrate the source twice, under different UFL degree estimates: - the load vector inner(q, v)·dx (steady.py:106; transient.py:235/242) is estimated at degree 3 + 2 = 5; - source_power = ∫q·dx (steady.py:133–135; transient.py:258), which the transient balance divides by (:310–312), is estimated at degree 3. - For a general cosine those two integrals differ at quadrature-error level (predicted 1e-8 to 1e-6), which would read red against E_BAND / S2_GAUSS_BAND 1e-9. - Here they do not. create_box repeats one six-tet split per hex, so any per-cell rule is a composite rule periodic in x with period h_x. Over a full period (N_x h_x = 2A), Σ_j cos(θ₀ + 2πj/N_x) = 0 exactly. So ∫cos(πx/A) is 0 to round-off at any degree, and both integrals equal Q·V_h. - A half-period or phase-shifted profile loses this — a trap for any later step that changes the profile. - source_power/(Q·V_h) − 1 is printed (predicted ≤ 1e-13) so that a red (S2) / (E) can be read at once (see Negative result). - One module-scoped fixture, sep_m4. Each phase is clocked with flush=True, in this order: 1. Uniform control (U). _rung_p(M4, clk, DEGREE) builds the mesh and solves the uniform source by step 3's exact code path (:131–145). Then: - ex_u, _ = _exact_p(msh, _steady_ex()) and χ = _interior_chi(msh); - whole and interior _rel_p and θ_h(0) through evaluate_vector_field_parallel, as step 3 :205–218; - Gauss printed (a round-off print, excluded from (U)). 2. Separable steady solve on the same msh / ft: solve_steady_conduction(msh, ft, k=K_GEL, q=q_sep, h=H_GEL, t_inf=T_INF, robin_tag=ROBIN_TAG, degree=DEGREE).     §9 item 497 — 2026-10-16 (§10 chain P36, daily — provisional; lane 3 closed form)¶

    Drafted for the 2026-10-16 10:30 review. Rule (6): chain P's third and last provisional step since the 10-14 weekly (P34, P35, P36 — the cap). P33 (MAT-15 step 7, the ASTM box heated by F-clinical's SAR) is serial on C6, and chain C is parked (GEO-38 item 485 BLOCKED). P32 called itself "the first step toward C6's thermal half (a prescribed non-uniform source in the ASTM box)"; P34 / P35 settled the hand-off form. P36 is the source-shape half: the transverse profile a body coil's quasi-static field deposits in a long phantom, in closed form and at P2. No new target and no band moves: the anchors are step 1's INTERIOR_BAND, S2_GAUSS_BAND and E_BAND, imported from the gate modules, against a closed form, exactly as P32 / P34 / P35 used them.

    MAT-21 step 9: the gel box under the transverse quadratic source

    q(x, y, z) = 3Q·(y² + z²)/(B² + C²) = Q·[w_y (y/B)² + w_z (z/C)²], with w_y = 3B²/(B² + C²) = 2.868293 and w_z = 3C²/(B² + C²) = 0.131707.

    The source is uniform along the 650 mm axis x and quadratic in the two transverse axes. It is the sum of two separable sources. It is checked in numpy (W1), then solved by P2 FEM on step 3's m = 4 rung, steady and CN to t* (W2). This is a record; the glyph stays ✅.

    Why this source (physics, stated once; nothing here is asserted). - Orientation. In the F2182 placement the 650 mm axis lies along the bore: GEO-38 step 2 puts MAT-21's x on the coil axis, y (420 mm) horizontal and z (90 mm) vertical (GEO-38.md:354). So the transverse pair is MAT-21's (y, z), and B₁ rotates in the y–z plane. - The long-prism limit is exact. Take an infinitely long prism along x in a uniform B = (0, B_y, B_z)e^{jωt}, quasi-static (low induction number, displacement current neglected). Then E = E_x(y, z) x̂ with E_x = jω(B_z y − B_y z) solves Faraday's law exactly, for any cross-section: - ∇·E = 0 holds; - n·E = 0 holds on every side wall, because E is axial and the side-wall normals are transverse; - the axial constant vanishes, because the net axial current is zero on a symmetric section. - Under circular polarisation (B_z = ∓jB_y, |B_y| = B₁) the two terms are in quadrature, so |E_x|² = ω²B₁²(y² + z²). The SAR is ∝ y² + z² in absolute units. That fixes the weights at w_y : w_z = B² : C² once each term is written in (s/L)², so the 90 mm axis carries (C/B)² = 4.6 % of the y-term's power: 0.131707 / 3 = 4.39 % of the total. - Normalisation. The mean of (s/L)² is 1/3, and w_y + w_z = 3. So the mean source is exactly Q, ∫q dV = QV = 49.14 W as in steps 1–8, and the Gauss comparand Q·V_h is unchanged. - Not claimed. This is the transverse shape of the long-body limit, not the box's own EM SAR. A 650 × 420 mm box is not long. Near x = ±A the axial current must turn (n·J = 0 at the end faces), and at 64 / 128 MHz the wavelength in gel is comparable to the box. No EM is solved.

    Choice, and why (one paragraph). Two candidates were weighed. - Chosen: (a), the sum of the two transverse quadratics. It is the long-prism CP eddy SAR derived above, with its physical z-weight. Against P32 it introduces exactly one new ingredient: the projection of (s/L)² onto the Robin eigenfunctions. That ingredient is exercised on two axes of very different Biot number (y 3.50, z 0.75). The x axis keeps the landed C. Two further points favour it: - The source is a degree-2 polynomial, so both of the solvers' source integrals are exact on affine tets. The balance anchors therefore hold without P32's full-period crutch (MAT-21.md:1140–1141). - It is the first MAT-21 step whose source varies along y and z. P32's scope excluded "a y/z-varying profile" (MAT-21.md:1229). - Rejected: (b), the product Q·[1 − cos(πx/A)]·(transverse quadratic). It is still separable, but it changes two things at once. It also has no physical derivation: the long-body axial E falls toward the end faces, while P32's cosine rises there. Its only extra content is P32's landed x-coefficient multiplied in, which (c-src) on (a) does not need. - Is it assertable beyond P32? Yes, modestly; no band is needed. - A new closed-form projection E_n, checked against quadrature and against two reduced routes. Each route is independent of E on its own axis. - The FEM anchors under a two-axis transverse source. - A new discriminating control (c-z): the FEM against the series with the z² term dropped misses by ≈ 4.8 % (≈ 4.8× INTERIOR_BAND). So the record shows the solver resolves a 4.4 %-power term on the 90 mm axis. - It does not move a glyph. It is lane-3 supply for a drained queue, priced at P32's measured windows.

    Licence. §10 chain P36, provisional under rule (6) (PROJECT_PLAN.md:3850–3860). Insert them after robin_box_separable_transient_temperature (:2224–2237) and before the MAT-17 banner (:2240). No landed function is edited. - robin_slab_quadratic_coefficients(gamma) returns E_n, the projection of (s/L)² onto cos(γ_n s/L) on |s| ≤ L:

    E_n = 2[sin γ + 2 cos γ/γ − 2 sin γ/γ²]/(γ + sin γ cos γ).

- Derivation: ∫_{−L}^{L}(s/L)² cos(γs/L) ds = 2L[sin γ/γ + 2 cos γ/γ² − 2 sin γ/γ³], divided by ∫cos² = L(γ + sin γ cos γ)/γ.
- This form is valid at any γ and has no division by sin γ.
- At a Robin root (cot γ = γ/Bi) it equals **C_n(1 + 2/Bi − 2/γ_n²)**. That identity is checked in W1, not used in the code.

    • robin_box_quadratic_steady_temperature(x, y, z, *, half_widths, k, q, h, weights, t_inf=0.0, n_terms=(40, 40, 40), return_gradient=False).

      • The source is q·[w₀ + w_x(x/A)² + w_y(y/B)² + w_z(z/C)²], with weights = (w0, wx, wy, wz).
      • Build axes = _robin_box_axes(half_widths, k, h, n_terms, None), then the coefficient tensor in this order:

      T = w0 * _robin_box_c3(axes) + wx * _robin_box_c3(axes_Ex) + wy * _robin_box_c3(axes_Ey) + wz * _robin_box_c3(axes_Ez)

      where axes_Ed is axes with axis d's C replaced by E. - Then W = (q / k) * T / _robin_box_lambda(axes) (the association of :2144), evaluated by _robin_box_eval unchanged. - At weights = (1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0) this is bitwise robin_box_steady_temperature, because 1.0 * c3 == c3 and c3 + (±0.0) == c3. - robin_box_quadratic_transient_temperature(x, y, z, t, *, half_widths, k, q, h, rho_c, weights, t_inf=0.0, n_terms=(40, 40, 40), return_gradient=False). - It starts from θ₀ = 0, and computes W = T * ((q / (k * lam)) * (-np.expm1(-at))) (P32's :2236 order). - At unit weights it is bitwise robin_box_transient_temperature at t_init = t_inf. - The docstrings carry the derivation, the truncated Gauss identity h∮θ_N dA = qV[w₀ΠS_d + Σ_d w_d S″d Π{e≠d} S_e], with S″_d = Σ E_n sin γ_n/γ_n → 1/3, and Duhamel.     • Negative result. There is no PREDICTED RED: line; every assertion is predicted green. Any red: report the measurement and stop. Park the work on attempt/* and mark the item BLOCKED in the same commit (rule (d)).
    • (Q1) or (Q1b) red: the projection or its sign is wrong. Report max|ΔE| per axis and stop before W2.
    • (Q2) red with (Q1) and (Q5) green: the association order differs. Fix it to the landed order and re-run W1 (rule (i)).
    • (Q3)–(Q6) red: report, stop before W2, and park, BLOCKED.
    • (Pdeg) red: print the counts and stop.
    • (U) red with everything else green: a determinism finding (the item 423 precedent). Park; the review rules; no band moves.
    • (S2-quad) or (E-quad) red: read source_power/(Q·V_h) − 1 first.
      • At the same level, the polynomial-exactness argument failed. That would be a UFL degree-estimation finding: write a known-issues entry.
      • At round-off, it is a scheme finding.
      • Either way, report and park.
    • (S1-quad) or (T-quad) > INTERIOR_BAND with (U) green: a finding on a y/z-varying source. Write a known-issues entry and park (rule (f): no band moves).

    MAT-21 step 11: P36's source under MAT-17's χ. The closed form is the ten-run Duhamel sum of P36's quadratic step response. It is checked in numpy (W1), then read against P2 CN to t* on m = 4 (W2). - Executor: implementer. - Tier: - W1 standard (numpy, real build, no mpiexec); - W2 heavy (-n 2, complex). - Measured bases: - P36 W1: 16 s harness (20261016T171632Z_MAT-21-step9-W1-closed-form.log). - P36 W2: 126 s; its CN runs 31.7 s, ex_t + ex_ut 30.5 s (20261016T171904Z_MAT-21-step9-W2-quadratic-fem.log:81–82). - Step 4 W3 (scheduled P2 duty CN on m = 4): 31.5 s (20261014T184606Z_MAT-21-step4-W3-p2-closed-form.log:89–90). - Class: lane 3, a chain step with solves. Cost: ≈ 7.4 measured / ≈ 40 predicted slot-minutes (two modules ≈ 25, windows ≈ 6, journal ≈ 8). - Depends on: nothing. Steps 0, 2, 3, 4 and 9 are on main. - Family: step 11, attempt 1 of 4.

    The schedule and the closed form. - The schedule is step 2's, unchanged. Its pins are N = 40, DT_BOX = t*/40, HALF_T = 4 DT_BOX, D = 0.5 and T_SW = m·HALF_T for m = 0 … 9 (tests/validation/test_mat21_box_duty_closed_form.py:53–57). χ is _chi_box (tests/validation/test_mat21_box_duty_fem.py:86–88). - The closed form is θ_duty(t) = Σ_{t > t_m} (−1)^m θ_q(t − t_m), where θ_q is robin_box_quadratic_transient_temperature (analytical.py:2291–2304). - It costs one series call, not ten. The time factor is linear, so the sum collapses onto one coefficient tensor: - axes, T = _robin_box_quadratic_tensor(HALF, K, H, n_terms, WEIGHTS) (analytical.py:2256–2265); - lam = _robin_box_lambda(axes) (:2105–2108); - F = Σ_m (-1.0)**m * (-np.expm1(-(ALPHA * lam * float(t - t_m)))) over t > t_m, accumulated in m order and starting from the m = 0 term; - W = T * ((Q / (K * lam)) * F), which is P36's association at :2303; - then _robin_box_eval(W, x, y, z, axes, 0.0, False) (:2092–2102).

    Both doses are cem43 on the same 41-sample grid. cem43 is the exact integral of the piecewise-linear interpolant (ruling 318-1), and the interpolant of δθ never exceeds its sample maximum, so D_h/D_s is a dose-weighted mean of 4^δθ(t) ∈ [4^(−M), 4^(M)]: the exact bound is e^(ln 4·M) − 1, printed beside (Bd)(i). The weekly's linear form holds whenever δθ is not ≈ +M over nearly the whole dose-weighted span (see Traps).

    Traps already paid for. - (Bd)(i) is first order. The exact bound is e^(ln 4·M) − 1; the linear form is exceeded only if δθ ≈ +M over nearly the whole dose-weighted span, by at most (ln 4·M)²·e^(ln 4·M)/2 ≈ 5e-7 at M = 7e-4 K. A (Bd)(i) red by less than that excess with (Bd)(ii) green is a linearisation finding to report — never swap in the exponential form in-slot. - Same-batch bytes (item 537, POST-8 3b-ii-t2): a point sample's bytes depend on the batch it was evaluated in. HIST_PTS is the one batch, in one order, on every snapshot; item 567 re-evaluates exactly this batch. The n = 40 snapshot precondition compares like with like. - Complex build: cem43 raises on a nonzero imaginary part (test_mat20_cem43_closed_form.py:123–127); _probe_vals returns np.real values minus T_INF — pass T_INF + θ, never θ, and never a complex array. - The ±y points are on ∂Ω: P37's (V) was green at -n 1 / 2 (item 520 Outcome). A (V) red here is a POST-8 finding with a known-issues entry; points are never nudged inward in-slot. - (A2)'s 16-digit strings depend on the image's scipy / numpy: a string red with _rel(d18, ref) ≤ DOSE_BAR green and everything else green is a (1*) record-reconciler case, never a physics finding. - quad's default epsabs (1.49e-8) is far above the integrand (R^23 ≈ 1.4e-14): _quad_dose passes epsabs=0 — import it; pass epsabs=0 to the true-integral and (Win) quad calls too. - Snapshot memory: 41 × 116 025 complex values ≈ 76 MB per run; clear after the reads. - P36's source has no comparison and no metadata; the snapshot kwarg compiles no new form. ufl.max_value / ordering comparisons on complex operands do not compile — none is needed. - _probe_vals is collective: call it on every rank with the identical module-constant point array. - Two heavy windows never run at once; after any kill, pgrep -c python3 first. A plain timeout does not stop mpiexec — -k 30 is in both commands. A headless session never backgrounds a window.

    The cells are not equally informative, and the measured scaling says where the bound is tightest. On going from the continuous source to a duty schedule, the max pointwise miss M_p barely moves: ×1.13 / ×1.20 at the walls and ×0.95 at the centre, for D = 0.5 / 0.25. Meanwhile max θ_s falls to 0.51–0.55 (D = 0.5) and 0.26–0.28 (D = 0.25) of its continuous value. These come from P41's printed and P42's asserted readings against P39′'s. Headroom therefore shrinks by roughly the θ ratio. P5 starts at the smallest continuous headroom of the six points (5.04×, the 8-cell z direction), so P5 under D = 0.25 should land at ≈ 1.1–1.5×. That is the tightest cell anywhere in the matrix, and exactly where P43's journal hypothesis places "the first place two-step on-phases and coarse z resolution compound" (attempts.md:1750).     Traps already paid for. - Every inherited helper is grid-bound (T_GRID, N_MAIN, MID_T). Calling one on 81-row arrays either raises or silently integrates on the wrong times. Never edit the originals to add a grid argument. - N = 40 runs go through the imported _cn_snap and N = 80 through _cn_snap_n. A string red on default40 with every identity green is a determinism finding against P44, never a tolerance to widen. - Switch times are physical, k · DT_BOX, one tuple for both grids, never rebuilt as 2k · DT80 (P42's grid-ULP trap). χ uses DT_BOX at both Δt. Never evaluate χ at a switch time. - startup_half_steps = 2 at both Δt. At t*/40 the first D = 0.125 on-phase is the two backward-Euler half-steps. Do not change the start-up to make the grids "match". - Nothing is asserted across Δt. (X-grid) and (FEM-X) are printed. T_GRID80[2n] and T_GRID[n] may differ in the last ULP. - Same-batch bytes (item 537): two fixed batches, one call each per snapshot, at -n 2. - Equal mean power is a scale (×8). Never run the CN at 8q. - Print before assert in (Bd125-80). A P5 red must not hide the other eleven cells. - (Bd)(i) is first order (item 565 Traps). At ±x the ratio is predicted near 1. A red by less than the second-order excess (≈ ln 4·M_p / 2 relative), with (ii) green, is a linearisation finding to report, not a band to move. - P3–P5 lie on ∂Ω. A validity red is a POST-8 finding with a known-issues entry. Never nudge a point. - Snapshot memory: clear each run's snapshots before the next. - The rest is item 565's list: - real θ into cem43, T_INF + θ; - quad with epsabs = 0; - _probe_vals is collective; - -k 30; pgrep after a kill; - never background a window; two heavy windows never at once.

    Scope. MAT-20's operators and P39′'s (Bd) bound on series and FEM point histories at the six F2182 points, under P36's source at D = 0.125 on P38's period, P2 on m = 4, at two time steps, -n 2 only. Not claimed: - a Δt rate or order (two time steps are two points); - a law for the duty penalty; - other periods; a periodic state; re-basing to 37 °C; - a dose limit, compliance, tissue or an implant; - the -n 1 width; - any coil, EM or external check.

    §9 item 659 — 2026-10-27 (§10 P47a, chain P — MAT-21 step 19, the box from a non-uniform initial temperature; lane 3 closed form)¶

    Written by the 2026-10-27 03:00 daily review from the 10-26 weekly's P47a (PROJECT_PLAN.md §10 chain P). One fact the weekly's text did not have: every Robin-box helper uses even slab modes only (cos(γ s / L) with γ sin γ = Bi cos γ; robin_slab_eigenvalues, analytical.py:1874; _robin_box_basis, :2057), and robin_box_transient_temperature takes only a uniform t_init (:2148). θ₀ = g·z is odd in z, so its projection needs the odd family.

    Anchor — new closed forms, appended after the MAT-21 step 0 section (analytical.py:2038 onward, before MAT-17 at :2308; insertions only). - robin_slab_odd_eigenvalues(biot, n): the roots of γ cos γ = −Bi sin γ (odd modes sin(γ s / L)), one per interval ((n − ½)π, nπ), by brentq, in the pattern of robin_slab_eigenvalues. - robin_box_initial_gradient_temperature(x, y, z, t, *, half_widths, k, h, rho_c, g, t_inf=0.0, n_terms=40): θ(t) − t_inf for θ₀ = t_inf + g·z with the source off. Separation: the x and y factors carry only the zeroth-order projection of a constant (θ₀ is uniform in x, y), i.e. the even-mode coefficients of 1 (robin_slab_cosine_coefficients, :2173); the z factor carries the odd-mode projection of z on (−C, C): b_n = ∫ z sin(γ_n z / C) dz / ∫ sin²(γ_n z / C) dz, in closed form. Cite Carslaw & Jaeger §3.10 (the slab with radiation at both faces) for the odd family. - Box and gel: A_BOX, B_BOX, C_BOX = 0.325, 0.21, 0.045 m (test_mat21_box_closed_form.py:34); K, RHO_C, H, T_INF from test_mat15_finite_cylinder_closed_form.py:43–47. g = 10 K/m (a 0.9 K top-to-bottom gradient over 90 mm; printed as the fixture's choice, not a measured phantom value).

    Identities — new tests appended to tests/validation/test_mat21_box_closed_form.py (or a new module test_mat21_initial_gradient_closed_form.py if the existing one's fixtures do not fit; never edit an existing test). Bars as step 0 uses them (literal bars R0–R6 in that module; B1_BAND is not a MAT-21 name): - (Odd) each odd root satisfies its characteristic equation to ≤ 1e-12, one root per interval. - (Rob) the six face Robin residuals ≤ 1e-10, _face_residuals' pattern (:87, asserted at :110 / :115). - (IC) the L2 reconstruction of g·z at t = 0 by the z-series: error at n_terms = 160 ≤ ½ × the error at 40 (a convergence statement; z does not satisfy the Robin condition, so pointwise 1e-12 is out of reach). Print all truncations. - (Dec) θ(t → ∞) → t_inf to ≤ 1e-12 (the decaying sum underflows), as test_r5_limits (:281). - (Bal) ∫ρc(θ(t) − t_inf) dV + the cumulative wall flux to t equals ∫ρc(θ₀ − t_inf) dV at three times, ≤ 1e-10 (the Gauss check's bar, :200). For g·z the initial integral is zero by symmetry, so assert it at the truncation's precision and print the wall-flux integral separately (it is zero too: odd in z on the top and bottom faces cancel).     Ruling. The brief's (Edge) asked a bar on the raw jump that the brief's own evaluation form cannot meet at any finite N: θ = sθ_ss − Σ(aₙs − Aₙ)Xₙ = s·(θ_ss − Σ aₙXₙ) + Σ AₙXₙ, so a switch of s by Δs moves θ by exactly Δs·r_N, where r_N = θ_ss − Σ aₙXₙ is the series' truncation residual (6.6e-10 at N = 400; the step helper carries the same residual at t = 0⁺). The physical statement (edge continuity) is that the state does not jump, and that whatever does jump is exactly the known truncation residual. That is what the re-post asserts, at the same bar and the same 32 instants: - (Edge′a) max |A_R − A_L| / max |aₙ| == 0 (already asserted on the branch; read 0). - (Edge′b) max over the instants and Z_GEL of |(θ_R − θ_L) − Δs·r_N| ≤ EDGE_BAND = 1e-13 of θ_ss(0) (read 7.588e-16 on the branch). - The raw jump max |θ_R − θ_L| is printed as a record, labelled "the N = 400 truncation residual", beside r_N — never asserted. - The off-phase strict decay stays asserted, unchanged.

    This changes the assertion's form, not its bar: the same 1e-13 now bounds the quantity a truncated series can actually hold continuous (item 677's precedent: an assertion below the series' own floor re-posed to the form that expresses the identity, MAT-21.md "Review ruling 2026-10-27 18:00").     §9 item 712 — 2026-11-01 (§10 P51, lane 3 → chain P — MAT-21 step 24: the pre-equilibration bias against the wait; lane 3 closed form, smoke, numpy)¶

    Enumerated by the 10-31 weekly. Depends on nothing. Next: P52. Family P51, attempt 1 of 4.

    Route. New module tests/validation/test_mat21_pre_equilibration_closed_form.py, numpy. Superposition: θ(t; t_w) = θ_drift(t + t_w) + θ_sourced(t), with θ_drift = robin_box_initial_gradient_temperature through test_mat21_initial_gradient_closed_form._theta (g = G_GRAD, T∞ = 0 offset) and θ_sourced = robin_box_transient_temperature (MAT-21 step 0's, KW, HALF, SERIES_TERMS). PROBE_PTS and PROBE_LABELS imported from test_mat21_box_probe_points_fem.py. The bias at a point: b(t_w) = θ_drift(t* + t_w) / θ_sourced(t*). The wait grid: t_w ∈ {0, 0.5, 1, 2} / λ₁, with λ₁ the slowest odd-in-z mode's decay rate: the drift is odd in z, so its slowest mode is not step 0's.

    One execution detail, returned to the 11-02 weekly. Five of P37's six points lie in z = 0, where the odd drift is exactly zero (item 669's finding), so the ratio holds at P5 only, and five rows read 0 by symmetry. The slot asserts that as (Sym0): |θ_drift| ≤ 1e-13 g C at P0–P4, and prints the six-point table as the weekly asked. For the same reason the decay gate is read at P5 and at ADJ_PT = (0, 0, 0.9 C), so the gate has two points rather than one. That is a clarification, not a new target.

    Anchors (asserted). - (Sup) the two limits: the combined helper with q = 0 equals θ_drift(t + t_w), and with g = 0 equals θ_sourced(t), each ≤ B1_BAND; plus the time shift: θ_drift evaluated at t + t_w equals the series at t with its amplitudes advanced by e^{−λ t_w} mode by mode, ≤ B1_BAND. The problem is linear, so the shift is the only part that is not true by construction. - (Dec∞) on the first odd mode alone (n_terms = 1): the bias ratio over t_w ∈ {1/λ₁, 2/λ₁} is e^{−λ₁ · 1/λ₁} to B1_BAND. This is the rate identity free of every other mode. - (Dec), the weekly's gate as written, on the full series: R = [b(2/λ₁) / b(1/λ₁)] · e − 1, |R| ≤ B1_BAND, at P5 and ADJ_PT.

    (Dec) is expected red, and why. λ₁ = α(γ_z²/C² + γ_x²/A² + γ_y²/B²) with γ_z ≈ 1.94 at Bi = 0.75. The lateral modes barely separate from it: the second x mode adds ≈ 128 m⁻² to λ₁/α ≈ 1 907 m⁻², a factor e^{−0.067} over Δt_w = 1/λ₁, and the second y mode adds ≈ 300 m⁻², e^{−0.16}.     So the route, the schedule and the walled sourced sum hold. What is new on the red run is the drift term, _drift_1d: P62's h_eff (massless-wall) drift. Item 805 measured exactly what that term leaves out. The wall-capacity term in the drift at P5 at t* is +2.174e-02 K (FEM − h_eff, 20261104T060527Z_MAT-21-P63-W1b.log:74–84).     Ruling. 1. The red stands as measured. No band moves, and the comparand is not changed here. Choosing a comparand that carries the wall's heat capacity (a two-layer odd-mode drift, which the repo does not have, item 788), or re-posing (I) against item 805's FEM drift, is a target question. Item 805's own negative-result clause gave it to the 11-04 weekly. 2. The re-pose is a separating measurement (§9 rule (6): "a measurement that separates two readings"). "C33's JSON strings, (K) re-read equal" — the premise is false as worded, and the route is the tracked log. - C33's JSON (/workspace/logs/geo38/c33-1p5t-3t.json, gitignored by .gitignore:82 /logs/) is side() per entry plus the four ratio strings (test_geo38_c33_field_strength_reader.py:112–131, :317–318). They are read through C33's own route, the ans:11 page's parse_c6_log loaded by c33._load_page() (P83's route, test_mat21_field_strength_heating_closed_form.py:129–132), never a new regex. This is the §9 digest's "every new step's reader … parses its tracked log". - (K) is that re-read: c33.check_side on each side, the 36 tokens re-formatted .9e equal, and the host C6a node JSONs (c6-node-193.5996.json, c6-node-44.0525.json, which do carry the lattice) through c33.custody_json — custody only: absent prints "absent", never a red. 2. "P80's 10 g-ball sources, one per lattice point". Each lattice point i carries a uniform source on the ball B_i of radius r = c6._a10() (0.013365 m, …P80-W1.log:47) at its box point (p80._lattice()), with strength ∝ its SAR10g. Per deposited watt, q_i = w_i/V_B with w_i = SAR_i/Σ_j SAR_j. ρ, P_acc and the drive amplitude cancel exactly. 3. The closed form (derived here; no src/ edit). analytical.py has no ball source in the Robin box, and its box series are even-only. The construction is the box heat kernel integrated over the ball, split in time at s₀ (Ewald-style): - θ_i(x, t) = (1/ρc)∫₀^{s₀} P∞(|x − p_i|; s) ds + (V_B/k)·Σ_modes F(√Λ r)·Φ(p_i)Φ(x)/𝒩·[e^{−αΛs₀} − e^{−αΛt}]/Λ, for t ≥ s₀. - Modes: per axis a, b both families — even cos(γs/L), γ tan γ = Bi (robin_slab_eigenvalues, analytical.py:1874), 𝒩 = L(γ + sin γ cos γ)/γ (:2179); odd sin(γs/L), γ cot γ = −Bi (robin_slab_odd_eigenvalues, :2307), 𝒩 = L(γ − sin γ cos γ)/γ (:2341). Axis c: even only, because every ball centre and both c* sit at c = 0 (P80 asserted max |c| 0), so every odd-c term carries sin 0 = 0. Λ = Σ_d (γ_d/L_d)². - The ball factor is exact: a product mode is a sum of plane waves with |k|² = Λ, and the ball mean of e^{ik·y} is e^{ik·p}·F(|k|r), F(u) = 3(sin u − u cos u)/u³ — the identity P81's _ball_mean_end uses (test_mat21_end_source_probe_points_closed_form.py:127–132). - The short-time piece neglects the walls. Every ball is ≥ 0.031635 m from a face, so the image factor is ≤ exp(−(2·0.031635)²/(4αs₀)) ≈ e^{−69.7} at s₀ = 100 s (printed). P∞ is the probability that a 3D Gaussian of variance σ² = 2αs about x lies in the ball: for d > 0, ½[erf((r−d)/(σ√2)) + erf((r+d)/(σ√2))] + (σ/(d√(2π)))[e^{−(r+d)²/(2σ²)} − e^{−(r−d)²/(2σ²)}]; at d = 0, erf(w) − (2/√π)w e^{−w²}, w = r/(σ√2). It is integrated by scipy.integrate.quad(…, epsabs=0.0, epsrel=1e-13, limit=200) (_quad_dose's settings). - Truncation: per axis, keep γ/L up to α(γ/L)²s₀ ≥ 40. At s₀ = 100 s that is N = (180, 120, 30) per family (γ_N/L ≥ 1730 / 1780 / 2025 m⁻¹ against the 1670 m⁻¹ needed); the dropped tail is ≤ e^{−40}. - Contraction: with c = 0 everywhere the c-factor is 1/𝒩_c for every ball. So θ₂ = (V_B/k)·Σ_lmn T_lmn W_lm/𝒩_c,n, with W = A·diag(q)·Bᵀ and T = F(√Λ r)·e^{−αΛs₀}·(−expm1(−αΛ(t − s₀)))/Λ: one (2N_a)(2N_b)N_c tensor per (t, s₀). 4. "θ(c*, t*) per deposited watt at each field strength's own c*; the predicted 3 T / 1.5 T ratio printed as power share × shape part". SP = θ₃(c*₃)/θ₁.₅(c*₁.₅), both per deposited watt. Predicted lever = (s₃/s₁.₅)·SP, with s from the .9e tokens (P83's expression, :140). 5. (N-eq) "equal columns ⇒ the shape part is 1 (P83's case reproduced)" — read as mirror-equal. - The two c* are mirror images under (a, b) → (−a, −b) (C33 …C33-W1-n1-r2.log:131), and so are the lattice and the box. - Literally equal columns do not give 1: the 1.5 T column on both sides gives SP ≈ SAR₁.₅(x+105mm dz+50mm)/SAR₁.₅(x−105mm dz−50mm) = 1.349823646/1.378896513 = 0.978916 (…C6.log:12304, :12291), plus neighbour terms. This is printed. - The asserted control is the mirror-equal column (the 3 T weights := the 1.5 T weights at the mirrored label) and the flat column (all w = 1/18, P83's even-source case). Both must give SP = 1.

    Diagnosis of attempt 1 (from the code and W1; no new run).

    1. Why the direct [0, t*] series is algebraic. At an even root, γ sin γ = Bi cos γ gives sin γₙ ≈ ±Bi/γₙ for large n. So both factors are small:
    2. c_n = 2 sin γ/(γ + sin γ cos γ) ≈ 2Bi/γ²;
    3. the box mean sin γ/γ ≈ Bi/γ².

    Then a_n = c_n·sin γₙ/γₙ ≤ 2Bi²/(γ³(γ − ½)), which is ∝ γ⁻⁴ and positive. Item 991's "sin γ/γ ≈ 1/n" was wrong.

    Every mode with αΛt* ≫ 1 has a saturated time factor (1 − e^{−αΛt})/Λ → 1/Λ ≤ L_d²/γ_d². So the tail of the [0, t*] series is the steady series' tail: terms ∝ γ⁻⁶ per axis, and a tail ∝ N⁻⁵.

    Item 991 posed no time split. Its claim of absolute convergence is true, but it does not reach 1e-12 at the brief's N.

    Splitting off the steady part does not help. The 3D Robin-box steady mean Σ Π a_d/Λ has no elementary closed form; it is the algebraic series. The cure is a split in time at s₀. On [s₀, t*] every mode carries e^{−αΛs₀}, and the [0, s₀] piece takes a short-time closed form. P89 already does this for (b).

    1. The rigorous tail bound for (a), stated. All a_n > 0, Σ_n a_{d,n} = 1 (the box mean of 1), 1 − e^{−x} ≤ 1, and 1/Λ ≤ L_d²/γ_d². Together these give

    T(N) = (1/(kV))·Σ_d Σ_{n>N_d} 2Bi_d² L_d² / (γ_n⁵(γ_n − ½)), γ_n ≥ (n − 1)π,

    an upper bound on direct(∞) − direct(N) per deposited watt. Drafter arithmetic, relative to ⟨θ⟩_u:

    N bound T(N) measured gap to the split value

    (80, 80, 80) 1.285e-09 1.282e-09
    (360, 240, 60) 3.059e-12 3.055e-12

    Anchor (closed form, named with its function). Unchanged target: item 991's ⟨θ⟩(t*) under (a) and (b), now through these forms. - (a) Uniform, s₀-split. This rests on an exact product identity. The box survival S(x, τ) under unit initial temperature with Robin faces is Π_d S_d(x_d, τ). Its box mean is Π_d M_d(τ), with M_d(τ) = Σ_n a_{d,n} e^{−α(γ_n/L_d)²τ} (the module's even axis, robin_slab_eigenvalues). Duhamel then gives ⟨θ⟩_u(t) = (q/ρc)∫₀ᵗ Π_d M_d dτ. Split at s₀ = p89.S0 = 100 s:

    ⟨θ⟩u(t) = (q/ρc)·I_s + (q/k)·Σ{N₀} Π_d a_d · e^{−αΛs₀}·(−expm1(−αΛ(t − s₀)))/Λ.

    The modal piece is the module's _tfac(…, s0=S0). I_s = ∫₀^{s₀} Π_d M_d^{sh}(τ) dτ.

    M_d^{sh}(τ) = 1 − [erfcx(x) − 1 + 2x/√π]/Bi_d, with x = (h/k)√(ατ). This is the slab mean with each face treated as a semi-infinite Robin solid: surface temperature erfcx(x), with heat lost ∫hθ_s dτ. Its image correction is ≈ e^{−L_d²/(αs₀)} ≤ e^{−141} on the thinnest axis.

    I_s is evaluated by 64-node Gauss–Legendre in u = √τ (dτ = 2u du) on [0, √s₀]. x ≤ 0.0632, so the integrand is analytic and its quadrature is exact to roundoff. Drafter: I_s ≈ 99.6540 s.
